surfaceIdsNote: The closed surface vocabulary of the whole orchestration family. The declaration schema, the policy-profile attestation, the SPEC-058 guard matrix and the SPEC-059 contracts use exactly these ids; the checker rejects any other spelling.
status: draft; documentation reading as of 2026-10-24; no host observation recorded; not an adoption

hostVersionsRead.versionBasis: minHostVersion is the first entry of the public Claude Code changelog (read-only reading of the repository CHANGELOG.md on 2026-10-24) that names the capability: agent teams 2.1.32 (research preview, experimental flag), /batch 2.1.63, agent view 2.1.139, claude agents --json 2.1.145, dynamic workflows 2.1.154 (as recorded for SPEC-052), cross-session SendMessage 2.1.224. It is a documentation reading, not a support claim for any version, and it is not a host observation.
hostVersionsRead.note: Documentation readings. A cell is only host-observed when it names a receipt created by a probe launched after the founder authorized it. SPEC-058's guard matrix may state a different minimum version for the same surface because it names a different capability (for example the TaskCreated hook, changelog 2.1.84, for agent-teams).

previewNote: Agent teams are experimental and off by default; agent view is a research preview; channels are a research preview. /batch details and the desktop session tools are not fully documented.

cells.capability: Declaration, expansion and pairwise evidence through analyze-work kind=aim or the CLI; isolation and base audit; agent() isolation-option lint
cells.notes: Whether workflow agents can call the plugin MCP is unconfirmed (SPEC-052 HV-1); the declared fallback is the orchestrating session or the CLI before the workflow starts. The isolation option list is documented only in the host's bundled authoring guidance.

cells.capability: Receipt at wave boundaries for committed or quiesced worktrees through the CLI; pull notice
cells.notes: Enforcement through hooks or permissions is SPEC-058. Bash writes and reads are not observed.

cells.capability: Read-only report for stopped or restarted agents from claude agents --json input, Git state and (best effort) the workflow journal
cells.notes: A resumed or restarted agent can re-apply edits over files other tracks touched; the journal is not a documented interface.

cells.capability: Planned reuse of the SPEC-052 braid-gate over committed work (SPEC-052 is unadopted and its host behavior is unobserved)
cells.notes: Unchanged by SPEC-057 and owned by SPEC-052. Replay certificates apply to at most four operations.

cells.capability: Plan-footprints step before launching sessions; isolation audit of shared working trees and base
cells.notes: Agent view is a research preview. Desktop session tool names are not in the public documentation and nothing depends on them.

cells.capability: Receipt at turn-end or idle checkpoints; epoch-stamped pull notice that the orchestrator reads and may relay through the host's own messaging
cells.notes: The Mailbox: a pull notice the orchestrator reads (the host wakes the orchestrator at the end of each turn of a linked session). Agent Braid never sends messages as a session. Whisper delivery is SPEC-058; Megaphone, Doorbell and a shared ledger are SPEC-059, behind G2.

cells.capability: Orphan report: observed worktree state versus claim, overlap with live siblings, warning before agent-view delete
cells.notes: Delete in agent view discards uncommitted work. No claim reclaim, resume or restart.

cells.capability: Branch tips of isolated sessions as possible commit sources for the SPEC-052 gate, inferred only; no SPEC-057 behavior is added at this point
cells.notes: Inferred, not documented or observed: whether a session's branch tip is a usable commit source is unconfirmed. Integration is owned by SPEC-052. The documented recipe may use the pairwise pre-flight matrix to choose which subset of at most four units is certified first; the rest are listed as uncertified.

cells.capability: Team plan check from per-task footprints submitted before spawning; shared-tree stale-read hazard flagged
cells.notes: Experimental and off by default. TaskCreated-based enforcement is SPEC-058 and fires only when the task tools are present, a documented rule whose presence on the model in use is unconfirmed (HV-7).

cells.capability: Shared-tree change inventory at quiescent points: every changed path is an unattributed writer with unknown effect; no per-unit comparison and no attribution to any teammate; lists beyond their bound are truncated and recorded, not refused; guard outputs are SPEC-058
cells.notes: One working tree: Git cannot attribute a write to a teammate, so the receipt cannot say who wrote what; it only inventories changed paths against the union of declarations. A busy tree yields a partial receipt with truncations, never a refusal and never a clean result. Orchestrator, human and shared-tree edits are unattributed writers reported as unknown unless a declared exemption rule excludes them. No PostToolUse Bash observer is specified.

cells.capability: Best-effort orphaned-claim report from Git state and, only if HV-12 passes, the task directory
cells.notes: In-process teammates are not restored by resume; the task directory is not a documented interface and the report fails soft.

cells.capability: No commit sources exist on a shared tree; no integration capability is specified
cells.notes: Whether an attributed-write ledger serves agent teams is decided after probe HV-L7 (SPEC-059); otherwise guidance is documentation plus per-teammate checkpoints committed by the lead, which is advisory only.

cells.capability: Plan lint at plan approval: declared footprints with required reads, shared-resource conventions, base check, isolation lint
cells.notes: The host has no hook at /batch plan approval; the lint is invoked by the user or the orchestrator. The decomposition and layout are not fully documented. Whether G1 includes a pre-flight arm for batch is decided after HV-11 and before the freeze (T043).

cells.capability: Receipt per unit at quiescent points; coalesced digest
cells.notes: Whether hooks fire inside /batch units is inferred; hooks are SPEC-058.

cells.capability: Classify each unit untouched, dirty, published, conflicting or unknown; flag worktrees with unrecorded work before deletion
cells.notes: /batch is not documented as resumable. Version 2.1.145 is the claude agents --json floor; /batch itself is 2.1.63.

cells.capability: Published branch tips as commit sources for the SPEC-052 gate, only if the undocumented layout maps to commit sources
cells.notes: Not covered. SPEC-052 does not mention /batch today. Until probe HV-11 records the branch and publication layout, nothing is claimed; if the layout maps to commit sources, a SPEC-052 extension would have to be specified, reviewed and recorded as a separate change, and no SPEC-057 behavior is added.

cellStatusesNote: reuse-of-SPEC-052-unverified means that the SPEC-052 read-only integration gate over commit sources is the intended integration evidence for the surface. SPEC-052 is an unadopted specification whose host behavior (HV-1 to HV-5) is unobserved, takes commit sources only, and has no surface id; the cell is a plan to reuse it, not a coverage claim, and it becomes covered only when the SPEC-052 evidence exists.
